Guides / 02—08

Seam allowances and hems do different jobs

Joining two pieces differs from folding a visible outer edge. Plan each edge as part of the pattern.

Vijeron · Updated 9 October 2026

Allowances belong to joins

A seam allowance provides space to stitch two edges. Its width depends on the pattern, fabric and finishing method; no single number suits every project. Mark the stitching line and how pieces meet. If a panel has a join on both sides, add space at both sides.

Hems belong to outer edges

A hem folds a fabric edge for a tidy finish and to control fraying. A double-fold hem needs material for both folds; it does not automatically equal the seam allowance. Decide each fold depth before sizing the cut piece, then test on a scrap to see how bulky it becomes.

List every edge

Draw a rectangle and label each edge: seam, hem or another treatment from the pattern. Add material only where required. If the finishing method changes, calculate the cut dimensions again.

Worked example

A panel 40 cm wide when finished, with a 1 cm seam on the left and two 1 cm hem folds on the right, needs a 43 cm cut width.

Pitfall to avoid

Do not replace a double-fold hem with one seam-allowance number without accounting for both folds.
